extracted.intended_audience: readers of entertainment industry news, SNL fans, and comedy/television followers
extracted.subtask_description: A short-form entertainment news article reporting Jay Pharoah's departure from Saturday Night Live, including quotes from the comedian and reader comments that evaluate aspects of comedic performance and industry practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impersonation versus comedic effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: “Impersonating someone is one thing — being funny while doing it is entirely another skill level.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes technical accuracy of an impression from the comedian's ability to make it funny; implies a quality standard that impressions should include comedic interpretation and not only mimicry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on writers as a marker of performer ability
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment: “If he needs a writer to be funny than he’s in the wrong game, sweetheart….”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expresses the evaluative stance that a sketch/satire performer should be able to generate or deliver humor independently; positions dependence on writers as a potential weakness (note: this is an audience/commentary view, not an objective rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Typecasting and being 'put into boxes'
rubrics_metrics.description: Quote from Pharoah: “They put people into boxes. Whatever they want you to do, they expect you to do.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as a criterion for evaluating a show's use of talent: whether performers are given varied opportunities or are constrained to narrow roles; implies underuse or miscasting reduces perceived value and career satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underutilization as a professional shortcoming
rubrics_metrics.description: Article reports Pharoah felt underutilized during his SNL run, contributing to dissatisfaction and eventual departure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames 'being underused' as a negative outcome for performers — a factor by which cast decisions and career moves can be judged; connects creative opportunity to retention and success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speaking out on representation may carry career risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Pharoah nearly lost his job for speaking out about the lack of black female cast members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers an implicit standard for industry behavior: advocating for diversity can be professionally risky, and such advocacy is a factor in evaluating the dynamics between talent and producers.
